test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 25 Jan 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.**
solution:
The correct answer is: **Start**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Start**" is a verb that refers to the beginning or initiation of an action, process, event, or state.
 
• "**Start**" is used as the base form of the verb.
 
 
• **Example**: *I start my car every morning.*
 
 
 
• In the given context of the sentence, "**start**" is the correct choice for the blank, and using the base form of the verb is appropriate because it follows the modal verb "**would not**."
 
• When using a modal verb like "**would**," the **base form of the main verb** is used.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• "**Started**" is used as the past tense of the verb.

 
 
• **For example**: *She started her new job last week.*
 
 
 
• "**Starting**" is used as the present participle (used in present continuous or gerund forms).
 
 
• **For example**: *They are starting the project today.*
 
 
 
• "**Starts**" is used when referring to the third person singular (he, she, it) in the present tense.
 
 
• **For example**: *He starts his work early in the morning.*
 
 

*​* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• The choice between "**start**" and "**starts**" depends on the grammatical structure of the sentence and the **subject-verb agreement**.
 
• In this case, "**start**" is the base form of the verb, and it agrees with the structure dictated by the past tense modal "**would not**."
 
• Using "**starts**" (as '**he**', the third-person singular form is mentioned) in this context, would create a **disagreement in verb tense**.
